verdict.rationale: Luma's own docs say its video model supports a character reference input, and that Luma Agents carry "style references, character references, and visual grounding into every asset" so the brand "holds steady." That is a first-party claim of consistency across multiple outputs, not just a reference input for one clip. The claim is marketing-level, though, and nothing hands-on shows the same character or scene holding across separately generated shots. Multi-Keyframe works only inside a single clip, and the community complaint about poor temporal coherence concerns within-clip quality rather than cross-shot consistency, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: detailed docs on how character/scene references persist across separate generations, documented limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration of cross-shot consistency.

support.subject: As a creator, a character or scene stays consistent across multiple generated shots, not just within one clip
